title: The War Named After An Ear
description:
The War of Jenkins' Ear (1739-1748) between Britain and Spain is named after Robert Jenkins, a British sea captain whose ear was allegedly cut off in 1731 by a Spanish coast guard captain who was searching his ship, which had been carrying smuggled sugar. In 1738 opposition politicians used the incident to build support for war. The capture of Portobelo in 1739 was celebrated with 'Rule Britannia' (written in 1740), and Portobello Road in London is named after it.

Source: Wikipedia, "War of Jenkins' Ear". Historians say trade and colonies mattered as much as the ear.
